step_by_step_reasoning: The whiteboard shows 'The Grid' data platform of Majid Al Futtaim. Nodes are transcribed from the 9 entities in the world model: web front-end user, EKS (Meta Manager microservices), Multiple Data Sources, Elastic Search & Neo4J (MetaStore), Vertica, S3 data lake, MSK (Kafka), RDS, and EMR. No fusion or expansion was needed; the Applications and DA/DS icons are not in the entity inventory and the ledger maps their arrows onto the existing endpoints, so no extra nodes were invented. Flows: flow 0 = metadata discovery (data sources -> Meta Manager on EKS -> MetaStore); flow 1 = collection into the data lake (data sources -> Kafka/EMR -> S3); flow 2 = processing and consumption (S3 <-> Kafka/EMR, EMR -> RDS and Vertica); flow 3 = connecting back to applications/users (bidirectional EMR <-> web consumer). Ledger self-check: visual_connections contains 14 entries and I emit 14 edges, one per entry, keeping the same source and target, including both directions and repeated pairs (S3 -> EMR twice, EMR -> S3 twice).

graph.name: Majid Al Futtaim - The Grid: Enterprise Data Platform
graph.notes: Data platform called 'The Grid' built around three pillars: collect, protect and connect data. Infrastructure is fully defined as code by the DevOps team and can be spun up and down on demand (e.g., for integration tests); first MVP in production in six months. Provides a 360 view of customers across businesses (e.g., Vox Cinemas and Carrefour) enabling cross-marketing campaigns and push notifications.

nodes.name: UserConsumerWeb
nodes.notes: Front end / consuming applications and users that connect to the platform; data is brought back to the business (e.g., loyalty application push notifications).

nodes.name: EKS
nodes.notes: Meta Manager: the brains of the Grid, running as a microservice architecture on EKS. Abstracts the complexity of the technology needed to move data, discovers tables, schemas and APIs, and applies data protection rules.

nodes.name: Multiple Data Sources
nodes.notes: Data sources spread across different networks, countries and technologies (tables, schemas, APIs).

nodes.name: Elastic Search & Neo4J
nodes.notes: MetaStore: combination of document and graph database storing the discovered meta information.

nodes.name: Vertica
nodes.notes: Data store for consumption by data analysts and data scientists (traditional analytics, models); data can be published or consumed via APIs.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Centralized data lake; around 60 terabytes of data. All data is stored in S3.

nodes.name: MSK
nodes.notes: Kafka enterprise streaming platform shared across all companies: 600 topics, 250 gigabytes, seven-day average retention period.

nodes.name: RDS
nodes.notes: Data store for consumption by data analysts and data scientists; data can be published or consumed via APIs or OLTP.

nodes.name: EMR
nodes.notes: Used in combination with Kafka to bring data into the data lake and to process data going in and out of it.

edges.notes: Meta Manager discovers which tables, schemas and APIs exist in the data sources.
Discovered meta information is stored in the MetaStore (document and graph database).
Data from the various sources is streamed into Kafka.
Data from the various sources is brought in using EMR.
Kafka streams the data into the S3 data lake.
EMR writes collected data into the S3 data lake.
Data goes out of the data lake to Kafka.
EMR reads data out of the data lake for processing.
Processed data is written back to the data lake.
Data is read from the data lake to be sent to the consumption data stores.
Data is sent to RDS for consumption by data analysts and data scientists.
Data is sent to Vertica for consumption by data analysts and data scientists.
Data from applications (also consumed through APIs) comes into the platform.
Data is brought back to the business applications to connect with users (e.g., push notifications and offers).
